title.zh: 卷六十七 唐書43: 列傳19 豆盧革 韋說 盧程 趙鳳 李愚 任圜
title.en: Volume 67 Book of Later Tang 43: Biographies 19: Dou Luge, Wei Shou, Lu Cheng, Zhao Feng, Li Yu, Ren Huan
title.raw: 卷六十七 唐書43: 列傳19 豆盧革 韋說 盧程 趙鳳 李愚 任圜 Volume 67 Book of Later Tang 43: Biographies 19: Dou Luge, Wei Shou, Lu Cheng, Zhao Feng, Li Yu, Ren Huan

sentences.zh: 豆盧革，祖籍，同州刺史。

translations.literal: Dou Luge; ancestral register; Tongzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge — a forebear in his line had served as prefect of Tongzhou; the ancestral name is not preserved in the received text.

sentences.zh: 父瓚，舒州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zan was prefect of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zan was prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宣和書譜》云：失其世係。）〉

translations.literal: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue states: his genealogical line is lost.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Xuanhe Calligraphy Catalogue notes that his pedigree is lost.)〉

sentences.zh: 革少值亂離，避地鄜、延，轉入中山，王處直禮之，辟於幕下，有奏記之譽。

translations.literal: Ge in youth encountered turmoil and dispersal, fled to Fu and Yan, then moved into Zhongshan; Wang Chuzhi treated him with courtesy and recruited him to his staff, where he won renown for memorials and letters.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Ge lived through war and exile, taking refuge in Fu and Yan before moving on to Zhongshan. Wang Chuzhi honored him and brought him onto his staff, where he gained a reputation for polished memorials and dispatches.

sentences.zh: 因牡丹會賦詩，諷處直以桑柘為意，言甚古雅，漸加器仰，轉節度判官。

translations.literal: At a peony gathering he composed a poem, admonishing Chuzhi with mulberry and ramie as his theme; his language was very antique and elegant, and Chuzhi came increasingly to esteem him, promoting him to military commissioner adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: At a peony festival he wrote a poem that, through mulberry and ramie, gently admonished Chuzhi. The verse was so refined and archaic in tone that Chuzhi came to esteem him ever more highly and promoted him to adjutant of the military commission.

sentences.zh: 而理家無法，獨請謁處直，處直慮布政有缺，有所規諫，斂版出迎，乃為嬖人祈軍職矣。

translations.literal: Yet in managing his household he had no discipline; he alone requested audience with Chuzhi. Chuzhi, fearing a gap in his governance, went to remonstrate; Ge folded his tablet and came out to meet him — only to beg a military post for a favorite.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he ran his household without discipline. When he alone sought an audience with Chuzhi, the lord, worried that his own governance might be at fault, came to remonstrate with him. Ge put away his tablet and came out to receive him — only to ask a military appointment for a favorite.

sentences.zh: 天祐末，莊宗將即位，講求輔相，盧質以名家子舉之，征拜行台左丞相。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianyou era, as Emperor Zhuangzong was about to accede, he sought chief ministers; Lu Zhi recommended him as a son of an eminent house, and he was summoned and appointed Left Chief Minister of the Mobile Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianyou reign, as Emperor Zhuangzong prepared to take the throne, he looked for chief ministers. Lu Zhi recommended Ge as a scion of a great house, and he was summoned and appointed Left Chief Minister of the Mobile Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 同光初，拜平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tongguang era he was made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 及登廊廟，事多錯亂，至於官階擬議，前後倒置，屢為省郎蕭希甫駿正，革改之，無難色。

translations.literal: Once he reached the halls of state, affairs were often confused; as to proposals for ranks and offices, earlier and later were reversed. He was repeatedly corrected by Secretariat officer Xiao Xifu, and Ge amended them without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the highest councils, affairs were often in disorder; in drafting ranks and offices he would reverse precedence, and Secretariat officer Xiao Xifu repeatedly corrected him. Ge made the changes without show of resentment.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初定汴、洛，革引薦韋說，冀諳事體，與己同功。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first secured Bian and Luoyang, Ge recommended Wei Shuo, hoping he would understand court procedure and share the work with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first secured Bian and Luoyang, Ge recommended Wei Shuo, hoping that Shuo knew how the court worked and would share the burden of office with him.

sentences.zh: 說既登庸，復事流品，舉止輕脫，怨歸於革。

translations.literal: Once Shuo took office, he again busied himself with pedigree grades; his conduct was careless and frivolous, and resentment was laid at Ge's door.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuo took office he again occupied himself with pedigree and rank, and his manner was careless and flippant; public resentment fell on Ge.

sentences.zh: 又革、說之子俱授拾遺，父子同官，為人所刺，遂改授員外郎。

translations.literal: Moreover, both Ge's and Shuo's sons were given posts as Reminder, father and son serving in the same office — which people criticized; they were then changed to positions as outside members of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, both Ge's and Shuo's sons were appointed Reminders, father and son holding office together — a thing people ridiculed — so their posts were changed to outside Secretariat members.

sentences.zh: 革請說之子濤為宏文館學士，說請革之子升為集賢學士，交易市恩，有同市井，識者醜之。

translations.literal: Ge requested that Shuo's son Tao be made an academician of the Hongwen Institute; Shuo requested that Ge's son Sheng be made an academician of the Jixian Institute — trading favors like marketplace haggling; men of judgment despised them.
translations.idiomatic: Ge asked that Shuo's son Tao be made an academician of the Hongwen Institute; Shuo asked that Ge's son Sheng be made an academician of the Jixian Institute. They traded favors like peddlers in a market, and thoughtful observers were disgusted.

sentences.zh: 革自作相之後，不以進賢勸能為務，唯事修煉，求長生之術；

translations.literal: After Ge himself became chief minister, he did not make promotion of the worthy and encouragement of talent his business, but devoted himself only to refinement and cultivation, seeking the art of long life;
translations.idiomatic: After Ge himself became chief minister, he did not make recommending the worthy and encouraging ability his concern, but devoted himself solely to alchemical refinement in search of the art of long life;

sentences.zh: 嘗服丹砂，嘔血數日，垂死而愈。

translations.literal: He once took cinnabar and vomited blood for several days, nearly dying before he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He once ingested cinnabar, vomited blood for days, and was near death before he recovered.

sentences.zh: 天成初，將葬莊宗，以革為山陵使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, when Zhuangzong was to be buried, Ge was made commissioner for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng, as Zhuangzong was to be interred, Ge was appointed commissioner for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 及木主歸廟，不出私第，專俟旄鎮，數日無耗，為親友促令入朝。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablet returned to the temple, he did not leave his private residence but waited solely for a border commission; after several days without word, kinsmen and friends urged him to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: When the spirit tablet had been installed in the ancestral temple, he stayed in his private house, waiting only for a frontier command. After days without news, relatives and friends pressed him to go to court.

sentences.zh: 安重誨對眾辱之曰：「山陵使名銜尚在，不候新命，便履公朝，意謂邊人可欺也。」

translations.literal: An Chonghui insulted him before the assembly, saying: "The title of tomb commissioner is still on you; without awaiting a new appointment you tread the public court — as if you thought men of the frontier could be deceived."
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui humiliated him before the court, saying, "You still bear the title of tomb commissioner. Without waiting for a new appointment you walk into open court — as though you thought a man from the marches could be fooled."

sentences.zh: 側目者聞之，思有所中。

translations.literal: Those who looked askance heard this and thought to find something to hit him with.
translations.idiomatic: Those who already watched him with suspicion heard this and looked for a chance to strike.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭希甫有正諫之望，革嘗阻之，遂上疏論革與說苟且自容，致君無狀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Xifu had hopes of straight remonstrance; Ge had once blocked him, so he submitted a memorial accusing Ge and Shuo of making shift for their own comfort and serving the ruler without proper form.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiao Xifu had hoped for a post as straight remonstrator; Ge had once blocked him. He now submitted a memorial charging Ge and Shuo with making shift for their own comfort and serving the ruler without due propriety.

sentences.zh: 復誣其縱田客殺人，冒元亨上第。

translations.literal: He further charged that Ge let his tenant retainers kill people and fraudulently claimed top rank in the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He further accused Ge of letting tenant retainers commit murder and of fraudulently claiming first place in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 遂貶為辰州刺史，仍令所在馳驛發遣。

translations.literal: Ge was therefore demoted to prefect of Chen and ordered dispatched post-haste from his post.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was therefore demoted to prefect of Chen and ordered sent off immediately by post relay from wherever he was.

sentences.zh: 後鄭玨、任圜等連上三章，請不行後命，乃下製曰：「豆盧革、韋說等，身為輔相，手握權衡，或端坐稱臣，或半笑奏事，於君無禮，舉世寧容。

translations.literal: Later Zheng Jue, Ren Huan, and others submitted three successive memorials asking that the later order not be carried out; then an edict was issued: "Dou Luge, Wei Shuo, and others, holding the posts of chief ministers and grasping the balance of power, sometimes sat upright and styled themselves subjects, sometimes reported affairs with a half-smile — discourteous to the ruler; could the world tolerate it?
translations.idiomatic: Later Zheng Jue, Ren Huan, and others submitted three memorials in succession asking that the later order not stand. An edict was then issued: "Dou Luge, Wei Shuo, and the like, as chief ministers holding the scales of power, would sometimes sit stiffly and call themselves subjects, sometimes report affairs with a half-smile — discourtesy to the ruler that the world could not abide.

sentences.zh: 革則暫委利權，便私俸祿，文武百辟皆從五月起支，父子二人偏自正初給遣。

translations.literal: Ge, for his part, temporarily delegated profitable authority and appropriated private salary and emoluments: all civil and military officials were paid starting from the fifth month, but father and son alone received disbursements from the first month.
translations.idiomatic: Ge, meanwhile, had temporarily delegated profitable authority and helped himself to salary and emoluments: every civil and military official was paid from the fifth month onward, but he and his son alone were paid from the first.

sentences.zh: 說則自居重位，全紊大綱。

translations.literal: Shuo, for his part, occupied a weighty post yet wholly disrupted the great framework.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo, for his part, held a weighty post yet threw the great administrative framework into disorder.

sentences.zh: 敘蔭貪榮，亂兒孫於昭穆；

translations.literal: Enfeoffing by inherited privilege from greed for glory, he confounded sons and grandsons in the order of the ancestral halls;
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for glory in granting hereditary privilege, he scrambled the proper order of sons and grandsons in the ancestral halls;

sentences.zh: 賣官潤屋，換令錄之身名。

translations.literal: selling offices to enrich his house, trading the personal names on orders and registers.
translations.idiomatic: sold offices to enrich his household and traded the personal names recorded on orders and registers.

sentences.zh: 醜行疊彰，群情共怒，雖居牧守，示塞非尤。

translations.literal: Vile conduct piled up in plain sight; common feeling raged together. Though they were placed in governorships, this showed remonstrance, not excessive blame.
translations.idiomatic: Their shameful conduct piled up in plain sight and public anger rose together. Though they were sent to regional governorships, this was meant to answer criticism, not as excessive punishment.

sentences.zh: 革可責授費州司戶參軍，說可夷州司戶參軍，皆員外置同正員，並所在馳驛發遣。」

translations.literal: Ge may be demoted and appointed Army Adjutant of Feizhou; Shuo may be Army Adjutant of Yizhou — both as supernumerary appointments with the same status as regular incumbents — and both dispatched post-haste from their posts."
translations.idiomatic: Ge is demoted to Army Adjutant of Feizhou; Shuo to Army Adjutant of Yizhou — both as supernumerary posts with regular status — and both are to be sent off immediately by post relay from wherever they are."

sentences.zh: 尋貶陵州長流百姓，委長吏常知所在。

translations.literal: Soon they were demoted to exiled commoners of Lingzhou, the chief local official charged always to know their whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they were reduced to long-term exiles registered as commoners of Lingzhou, with local chiefs ordered always to know where they were.

sentences.zh: 天成二年夏，詔令逐處刺史監賜自盡，其骨肉並放逐便。

translations.literal: In summer of the second year of Tiancheng, an edict ordered each prefect where they were to supervise and grant them death by their own hand; their kin were also banished forthwith.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Tiancheng an edict ordered the prefect of each place where they were held to supervise and grant them death by their own hand; their families were banished at once as well.

sentences.zh: 子升，官至檢校正郎，服金紫，尋亦削奪。

translations.literal: His son Sheng had reached the post of Secretariat proofreader, wore gold and purple, but was soon stripped of these as well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng had risen to proofreader in the Secretariat and wore gold and purple insignia, but these too were soon stripped from him.

sentences.zh: 〈（《寶晉齋法書讚》載豆盧革《田園帖》云：大德欲要一居處，畿甸間舊無田園，鄜州雖有三兩處莊子，緣百姓租佃多年，累有令公大王書請，卻給還人戶，蓋不欲侵奪疲民，兼慮無知之輩，妄有影庇包役云云。

translations.literal: (The Baojin Studio Calligraphy Eulogy records Dou Luge's "Letter on Fields and Gardens" stating: Great Virtue wishes to have a dwelling; in the capital region he formerly had no estates; in Fuzhou there are two or three manor farms, but because common people have rented and farmed them for many years, the Prince and Great King repeatedly sent letters requesting them, yet they were returned to the registered households — lest he seize from weary commoners, and also fearing that ignorant persons might falsely shelter and shield corvée labor, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: (The Baojin Studio Calligraphy Eulogy preserves Dou Luge's "Letter on Fields and Gardens," in which he writes that his correspondent Great Virtue wants a residence; he has no estate near the capital, and though Fuzhou has two or three manor farms, the common people have rented them for years. The Prince and Great King have repeatedly written to claim them, yet Ge returned them to the registered households — not wishing to seize from exhausted commoners and fearing that ignorant men might falsely shelter others to evade corvée, and so forth.

sentences.zh: 嶽珂曰：此帖乃與僧往還書，其畏強藩避罪罟，蓋栗栗淵冰，然其後卒以故縱田客貶夜郎，正坐所畏，信乎亂邦之不可居也。

translations.literal: Yue Ke says: This letter was correspondence with a monk; in fearing powerful feudatories and avoiding punishment, he was as cautious as treading on thin ice — yet in the end he was still demoted to Yelang for indulging tenant killers, exactly what he had feared; truly a chaotic age is no place to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ke comments: This letter was exchanged with a monk. In fearing powerful feudatories and avoiding the net of punishment he was as cautious as if treading on thin ice — yet in the end he was still banished to Yelang for indulging tenant retainers who killed, suffering precisely what he had feared. Truly, a chaotic age is no place to live.

sentences.zh: 是時據鄜乃高萬興，官檢校太師、中書令，封北平王，即革所謂「令公大王」者。

translations.literal: At that time the holder of Fu was Gao Wanxing, titular Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping — the "Prince and Great King" Ge meant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fu was held by Gao Wanxing, who bore the titular ranks of Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping — the "Prince and Great King" of whom Ge spoke.

sentences.zh: 官故梁授，唐命維新，而顓麵正朝者，不能致褫鞶之誅，而反竊貢秉旄之佞，唐之不競，有自來矣。）〉

translations.literal: His offices were inherited from Liang appointment; the Tang mandate was renewed, yet those who faced the court could not bring down the punishment of disgraceful girdle removal, but instead usurped tribute and grasped command batons — Tang's failure to compete had long been coming.)〉
translations.idiomatic: His offices had been granted under the Liang; though the Tang mandate was renewed, the court could not inflict the disgrace of stripping his girdle ornaments, while he usurped tribute and clutched a commander's baton — Tang's loss of vigor had been long in the making.)〉

sentences.zh: 韋說，福建觀察使岫之子也。

translations.literal: Wei Shuo was the son of Wei Zhou, Military Commissioner of Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuo was the son of Wei Zhou, military commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: text is missing below.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: the text below is defective.)〉

sentences.zh: 莊宗定汴、洛，說與趙光允同製拜平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong secured Bian and Luoyang, Shuo was made Grand Councilor together with Zhao Guangyun by edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong secured Bian and Luoyang, Shuo and Zhao Guangyun were appointed Grand Councilors by edict on the same day.

sentences.zh: 說性謹重，奉職常不造事端。

translations.literal: Shuo's nature was cautious and grave; in office he ordinarily stirred up no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was by nature cautious and grave; in office he usually stirred up no incidents.

sentences.zh: 時郭崇韜秉政，說等承順而已，政事得失，無所措言。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Chongtao held power; Shuo and the others merely complied, and as to gains and losses in government they had nothing to say.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao then held real power; Shuo and his colleagues only followed along and had nothing to say about what the government did right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 初，或有言於崇韜，銓選逾濫，選人或取他人出身銜，或取父兄資緒，與令史囊橐罔冒，崇韜乃條奏其事。

translations.literal: Earlier someone told Chongtao that selection and appointment had grown excessive: candidates would take another person's credentials and rank, or borrow a father or elder brother's qualifications, colluding with clerks who lined their purses in fraud. Chongtao then submitted a detailed memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had told Chongtao that appointments had grown wildly lax — candidates using others' credentials, borrowing fathers' or brothers' qualifications, while clerks took bribes to pass false claims. Chongtao then submitted a detailed memorial on the abuses.

sentences.zh: 其後郊天，行事官數千人，多有告敕偽濫，因定去留，塗毀告身者甚眾，選人號哭都門之外。

translations.literal: Later, at the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, among the several thousand officiating officials many had fraudulent or excessive patents of appointment; when retention and dismissal were decided, many appointment documents were defaced, and candidates wailed outside the capital gates.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, among thousands of ritual officers many held forged or improper commissions. When retention and dismissal were decided, countless appointment documents were defaced, and rejected candidates wailed outside the capital gates.

sentences.zh: 議者亦以為積弊累年，一旦澄汰太細，懼失惟新含垢之意。

translations.literal: Commentators also held that abuses had piled up for years, yet to purge them all at once in such fine detail feared losing the intent of renewal that tolerates faults.
translations.idiomatic: Critics also argued that abuses had accumulated for years, yet to purge them so thoroughly at a stroke risked abandoning the spirit of renewal that forgives past faults.

sentences.zh: 時說與郭崇韜國列，不能執而止之，頗遭物議。

translations.literal: Shuo then held equal rank with Guo Chongtao as chief minister but could not hold firm and stop it, and he drew considerable public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo then shared chief-ministerial rank with Guo Chongtao yet could not stand firm and stop the purge, and he drew considerable criticism.

sentences.zh: 說之親黨告之，說曰：「此郭漢子之意也。」

translations.literal: Shuo's kinsmen and associates informed him; Shuo said: "This is that Guo fellow's idea."
translations.idiomatic: When Shuo's kinsmen and associates told him of the criticism, he said, "This is that Guo fellow's doing."

sentences.zh: 及崇韜得罪，說懼流言所鍾，乃令門人左拾遺王鬆、吏部員外郎李慎儀等上疏，云：「崇韜往日專權，不閑故實，塞仕進之門，非獎善之道。」

translations.literal: When Chongtao fell from grace, Shuo feared slander would converge on him and had his protégés — Left Reminder Wang Song and Ministry of Personnel outside member Li Shenyi — submit memorials saying: "Chongtao in former days monopolized power, was unversed in precedent, blocked the gates of advancement, and this is not the way to reward the good."
translations.idiomatic: After Chongtao was condemned, Shuo feared gossip would turn on him and had his protégés — Left Reminder Wang Song and outside member of the Ministry of Personnel Li Shenyi — submit memorials saying, "Chongtao once monopolized power, ignored precedent, blocked the path of office, and did not reward merit as he should."

sentences.zh: 疏下中書，說等覆奏，深詆崇韜，識者非之。

translations.literal: The memorials were sent down to the Secretariat; Shuo and others replied in memorial, deeply denigrating Chongtao, and men of judgment disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials went to the Secretariat; Shuo and his colleagues replied with further denunciations of Chongtao, which thoughtful observers condemned.

sentences.zh: 又有王傪者，能以多岐取事，納賂於說，說以其名犯祖諱，遂改之為「操」，擬官於近甸。

translations.literal: There was also one Wang Can who could win favor by many crooked means and paid bribes to Shuo; because his name violated Shuo's ancestral taboo, Shuo changed it to "Cao" and proposed an office for him in the near capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: There was also a Wang Can who won favor by devious means and paid bribes to Shuo. Because his name violated Shuo's ancestral taboo, Shuo changed it to "Cao" and proposed an appointment for him in the districts near the capital.

sentences.zh: 及明宗即位，說常慮身危，每求庇於任圜，常保護之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong acceded, Shuo often feared for his person and repeatedly sought protection from Ren Huan, who regularly shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Shuo often feared for his life and repeatedly sought shelter from Ren Huan, who regularly protected him.

sentences.zh: 說居有井，昔與鄰家共之，因嫌鄙雜，築垣於外。

translations.literal: Where Shuo lived there was a well formerly shared with a neighbor; disliking the vulgar mingling, he built a wall outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo's residence had a well once shared with a neighbor; finding the mingling vulgar, he built a wall to shut it off.

sentences.zh: 鄰人訟之，為希甫疏論，以為井有貨財，及案之本人，惟稱有破釜一所，反招虛妄。

translations.literal: The neighbor sued; Xiao Xifu discussed it in a memorial, holding that the well held goods and wealth, but when the case was investigated Shuo himself said only that there was one broken cauldron — which instead invited the charge of falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbor brought suit. In a memorial Xiao Xifu argued that Shuo treated the well as a source of profit; when the case was examined Shuo himself could only point to a single broken cauldron — which made him look all the more false.

sentences.zh: 初貶敘州刺史，尋責授夷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was first demoted to prefect of Xu, then demoted and appointed Army Adjutant of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was first demoted to prefect of Xu, then stripped further and appointed Army Adjutant of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，說在江陵，與高季興相知，及入中書，亦常通信幣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shuo was at Jiangling, he was on friendly terms with Gao Jixing; after he entered the Secretariat he still often exchanged letters and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Shuo was at Jiangling, he knew Gao Jixing well; after he entered the chief minister's office he still exchanged letters and gifts with him.

sentences.zh: 自討西蜀，季興請攻峽內，莊宗許之：「如能得三州，俾為屬郡。」

translations.literal: From the campaign against Western Shu, Jixing asked to attack the inner gorges; Zhuangzong assented: "If you can take the three prefectures, they shall be made your subordinate commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Western Shu, Jixing asked to attack the gorges within the passes. Zhuangzong agreed: "If you can take the three prefectures, they shall be made your dependent commanderies."

sentences.zh: 西川既定，季興無尺寸之功。

translations.literal: When Western Shu was pacified, Jixing had not a finger's breadth of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Shu was pacified, Jixing had achieved nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 洎明宗纘承，季興頻請三郡，朝廷不得已而與之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong succeeded to the throne, Jixing repeatedly asked for the three commanderies, and the court, having no choice, granted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong succeeded, Jixing repeatedly demanded the three commanderies, and the court, unable to refuse, granted them.

sentences.zh: 革、說方在中書，亦預其議。

translations.literal: Ge and Shuo were then in the Secretariat and also took part in the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Ge and Shuo were then in the Secretariat and took part in the decision as well.

sentences.zh: 及季興占據，獨歸其罪，流於合州。

translations.literal: When Jixing seized and held them, the blame was laid on them alone and they were exiled to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jixing seized and held the territories, blame fell on them alone and they were exiled to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，詔曰：「陵州、合州長流百姓豆盧革、韋說，頃在先朝，擢居重任，欺公害物，黷貨賣官。

translations.literal: The next summer an edict said: "The long-exiled commoners Dou Luge of Lingzhou and Wei Shuo of Hezhou were lately raised to weighty posts in the former court, harmed the public and preyed on things, took bribes and sold offices.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer an edict declared: "The long-exiled commoners Dou Luge of Lingzhou and Wei Shuo of Hezhou were recently elevated to heavy responsibility under the former court, yet they cheated the public, preyed on the realm, took bribes, and sold offices.

sentences.zh: 靜惟肇亂之端，更有難容之事，且夔、忠、萬三州，地連巴蜀，路扼荊蠻，藉皇都弭難之初，徇逆帥僭求之勢，罔予視聽，率意割移。

translations.literal: Reflecting quietly on the source of disorder, there is still more that cannot be tolerated: moreover the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan border Ba and Shu and straddle the roads of Jing and the southern barbarians; taking advantage of the capital's first effort to quell trouble, they indulged a rebellious commander's overreaching demands, disregarded Our sight and hearing, and on their own authority ceded territory.
translations.idiomatic: On reflection, the seeds of disorder lie in deeds still harder to forgive: the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan border Ba-Shu and choke the routes into Jing and the south. Exploiting the capital's first efforts to restore peace, they bowed to a rebellious commander's grasping demands, ignored Our authority, and ceded territory at will.

sentences.zh: 將千之土疆，開通狡穴；

translations.literal: They would have opened a thousand li of territory to crafty lairs;
translations.idiomatic: They would have opened a thousand li of territory to treacherous strongholds;

sentences.zh: 動兩川之兵賦，禦捍經年。

translations.literal: mobilized the armies and revenues of the Two Shu, and for years on end had to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: and mobilized the armies and revenues of the Two Shu for years of defense.

sentences.zh: 致朕莫遂偃戈，猶煩運策。

translations.literal: This caused Us not yet to lay down Our weapons but still to trouble Ourselves with strategy.
translations.idiomatic: This kept Us from laying down Our arms and still forced Us to labor over strategy.

sentences.zh: 近者西方鄴雖復要害，高季興尚固窠巢，增吾旰食之憂，職爾朋奸之計。

translations.literal: Recently, though the western Ye stronghold was recovered, Gao Jixing still held fast to his nest, increasing Our worry that steals Our meals — the work of your faction of villains.
translations.idiomatic: Though the western stronghold of Ye was recently recovered, Gao Jixing still clings to his lair, deepening Our anxiety that steals sleep from Our meals — a plot of your villainous faction.

sentences.zh: 而又自居貶所，繼出流言。

translations.literal: Moreover, though you dwell in places of demotion, slander continues to issue forth.
translations.idiomatic: And though you sit in places of exile, slander still flows from you.

sentences.zh: 苟刑戮之稽時，處忠良於何地？

translations.literal: If punishment is delayed, where shall the loyal and good stand?
translations.idiomatic: If punishment is delayed, what place is left for the loyal and worthy?

sentences.zh: 宜令逐處刺史監賜自盡。」

translations.literal: Each prefect where they are shall be ordered to supervise and grant them death by their own hand."
translations.idiomatic: Let the prefect of each place where they are held supervise and grant them death by their own hand."

sentences.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：說子濤，晉天福初，為尚書膳部員外郎，卒。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang's History: Shuo's son Tao, at the beginning of Tianfu in Jin, was outside member of the Ministry of Rites, Provisioners Section, and died.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang Xiu's History of the Five Dynasties: Shuo's son Tao, early in the Jin Tianfu era, served as outside member of the Provisioners Section in the Ministry of Rites and died in office.)〉

sentences.zh: 盧程，唐朝右族。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng was of a great Tang house.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng came from a great Tang clan.

sentences.zh: 祖懿，父蘊，曆仕通顯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi and his father Yun both served in eminent and conspicuous posts.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi and his father Yun both held distinguished offices through their careers.

sentences.zh: 程，天復末登進士第，崔魏公領鹽鐵，署為巡官。

translations.literal: Cheng passed the jinshi at the end of Tianfu; when Duke Wei of Cui headed the Salt and Iron Commission, he appointed him an inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng passed the jinshi examination late in the Tianfu era. When Duke Wei of Cui headed the Salt and Iron Commission, he appointed Cheng an inspector.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，柳璨陷右族，程避地河朔，客遊燕、趙，或衣道士服，幹謁藩伯，人未知之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Liu Can ruined great houses; Cheng fled to Heshuo, traveled as a guest in Yan and Zhao, sometimes wore Daoist robes, and sought audiences with feudal lords — people did not yet know him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang and Liu Can brought down great families, Cheng took refuge in Heshuo and wandered as a guest in Yan and Zhao, sometimes wearing Daoist robes as he sought audiences with regional lords — and was still unknown.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革客遊中山，依王處直，盧汝弼來太原。

translations.literal: Dou Luge traveled as a guest in Zhongshan and relied on Wang Chuzhi; Lu Rubi came to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge wandered as a guest in Zhongshan under Wang Chuzhi; Lu Rubi came to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 程與革、弼皆朝族知舊，因往來依革，處直禮遇未優，故投於太原；

translations.literal: Cheng, Ge, and Rubi were all court-clan acquaintances of old; Cheng therefore went back and forth relying on Ge, but Chuzhi's courtesy was not generous, so he turned to Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, Ge, and Rubi were all old acquaintances from court families. Cheng therefore attached himself to Ge for a time, but since Chuzhi did not treat him generously he went on to Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 汝弼因為延譽，莊宗署為推官，尋改支使。

translations.literal: Rubi thereupon recommended him, and Zhuangzong appointed him investigating officer, soon changing the title to staff adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi recommended him, and Zhuangzong appointed him investigating officer, soon promoting him to staff adjutant.

sentences.zh: 程褊淺無他才，惟矜恃門第，口多是非，篤厚君子尤薄之。

translations.literal: Cheng was narrow and shallow, without other talent; he relied only on his pedigree, his mouth full of right and wrong, and earnest gentlemen especially despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was narrow-minded and shallow, with no other real talent; he prided himself only on birth and was quick to gossip. Men of solid character especially despised him.

sentences.zh: 初，判官王緘從軍掌文翰，胡柳之役，緘歿於軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, adjutant Wang Jian followed the army in charge of documents; in the battle at Huliu, Jian died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the adjutant Wang Jian had followed the army as chief secretary; at the battle of Huliu he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 莊宗歸寧太原，置酒公宴，舉酒謂張承業曰：「予今於此會取一書記，先以卮酒辟之。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong returned to pay respects at Taiyuan and set out wine at a public feast; raising his cup he said to Zhang Chengye: "I shall now at this gathering choose a secretary — first let this cup of wine announce it."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan for a family visit he held a public feast. Raising his cup to Zhang Chengye he said, "At this gathering I shall choose a secretary — let this cup announce my choice."

sentences.zh: 即舉酒屬巡官馮道，道以所舉非次，抗酒辭避。

translations.literal: He then raised his cup and assigned it to inspector Feng Dao; Dao, because the appointment was out of order, resisted the cup and declined.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered the cup to the inspector Feng Dao. Dao, finding the appointment out of proper sequence, refused the cup and declined.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「勿謙挹，無逾於卿也。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said: "Do not be modest — none surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "Do not be modest — no one is better suited than you."

sentences.zh: 時以職列序遷，則程當為書記，汝弼亦左右之。

translations.literal: At the time, by order of rank in office, Cheng ought to have been secretary, and Rubi too supported him.
translations.idiomatic: By seniority in office Cheng should have been secretary, and Rubi had been promoting him as well.

sentences.zh: 程既失職，私懷憤惋，謂人曰：「主上不重人物，使田里兒居餘上。」

translations.literal: Cheng, having lost the post, privately nursed resentment and said to others: "Our lord does not value men of quality, letting a village lad rank above me."
translations.idiomatic: Having lost the post, Cheng privately nursed resentment and told others, "Our lord does not value talent — he lets a village lad rank above me."

sentences.zh: 先是，莊宗嘗於帳中召程草奏，程曰：「叨忝成名，不閑筆硯。」

translations.literal: Earlier Zhuangzong had once summoned Cheng in his tent to draft a memorial; Cheng said: "I am unworthily famous but unskilled with brush and inkstone."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhuangzong had summoned Cheng to his tent to draft a memorial. Cheng said, "I am unworthily famous, but I am no hand with brush and ink."

sentences.zh: 由是文翰之選，不及於程。

translations.literal: From this the choice for literary duties did not reach Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on he was never considered for literary posts.

sentences.zh: 時張承業專製河東留守事，人皆敬憚。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Chengye monopolized control of the Hedong regent's affairs, and everyone feared and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye then controlled the Hedong regent's affairs single-handedly, and everyone feared him.

sentences.zh: 舊例，支使監諸廩出納，程訴於承業曰：「此事非仆所長，請擇能者。」

translations.literal: By old custom the staff adjutant supervised receipts and disbursements at the granaries; Cheng appealed to Chengye, saying: "This matter is not what your servant is good at — please choose someone capable."
translations.idiomatic: By custom the staff adjutant supervised granary receipts and disbursements. Cheng appealed to Chengye: "This is not my strength — please choose someone capable."

sentences.zh: 承業叱之曰：「公稱文士，即合飛文染翰，以濟霸國，嘗命草辭，自陳短拙，及留職務，又以為辭，公所能者何也？」

translations.literal: Chengye rebuked him: "You call yourself a man of letters — you ought to fly with prose and stain the brush to aid the hegemonic state. When ordered to draft a text you declared yourself clumsy; when left with duties you again make excuses — what can you do?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengye snapped at him: "You call yourself a scholar — you should wield the brush to aid our hegemonic enterprise. Ordered to draft a text you pleaded incompetence; left with duties you plead again — what are you good for?"

sentences.zh: 程垂泣謝之。

translations.literal: Cheng wept as he bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wept as he apologized.

sentences.zh: 後曆觀察判官。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as adjutant to military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as adjutant to several military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 及汴將王彥章陷德勝南城，爭攻楊劉，莊宗禦軍苦戰，臣下憂之，鹹白宰臣，欲連章規諫，請不躬禦士伍。

translations.literal: When the Bian general Wang Yanzhang took the southern city of Desheng and strove to attack Yangliu, Zhuangzong led the army in bitter fighting; his ministers were anxious and all told the chief ministers they wished to submit linked memorials urging him not to lead the ranks in person.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian general Wang Yanzhang captured the southern city of Desheng and pressed the attack on Yangliu, Zhuangzong led the army in bitter fighting. His ministers were alarmed and all urged the chief ministers to submit joint memorials asking him not to command the ranks in person.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革言及漢高臨廣武事，矢及於胸，紿雲中足。

translations.literal: Dou Luge spoke of how Emperor Gaozu of Han at Guangwu had an arrow reach his chest yet deceived the enemy that he had been struck in the foot.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge cited how Emperor Gaozu of Han, at Guangwu, took an arrow in the chest yet deceived the enemy into thinking he had been wounded in the foot.

sentences.zh: 程曰：「此劉季失策。」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "That was Liu Ji’s blunder."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "That was Liu Bang's mistake."

sentences.zh: 眾皆縮頸。

translations.literal: Everyone drew in his neck.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone shrank back in alarm.

sentences.zh: 嘗論近世士族，或曰：「員外郎孔明龜，善和宰相之令緒，宣聖之係孫，得非盛歟！」

translations.literal: Once when discussing recent gentry houses, someone said: "Outside member Kong Minggui of Shanhe — a descendant of a chief minister's line and a collateral of the Sage of Culture — is that not splendid!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, discussing recent great families, someone said, "The outside member Kong Minggui of Shanhe — descended from a chief minister's line and collateral kin of Confucius — surely that is splendid!"

sentences.zh: 程曰：「止於孔子之後，盛則吾不知也。」

translations.literal: Cheng said: "He only reaches to being a descendant of Confucius — as for being splendid, I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "He only amounts to being a descendant of Confucius — as for being splendid, I could not say."

sentences.zh: 親黨有假驢夫於程者，程帖府給之，府吏訴雲無例，程怒鞭吏背。

translations.literal: A kinsman had borrowed a donkey driver from Cheng; Cheng posted a note to the prefecture to supply one. A prefectural clerk complained that there was no precedent, and in anger Cheng whipped the clerk's back.
translations.idiomatic: A relative had asked Cheng to lend him a donkey driver; Cheng sent a note to the prefecture ordering one supplied. When a clerk protested that there was no precedent for it, Cheng flew into a rage and had the man flogged.

sentences.zh: 時任圜為興唐少尹，莊宗從姊婿也，憑其寵戚，因詣程。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Huan was Vice Mayor of Xingtang, a husband of one of Emperor Zhuangzong's older paternal cousins; relying on his favored kinship, he therefore went to see Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ren Huan served as Vice Mayor of Xingtang. As the husband of one of Emperor Zhuangzong's older cousins by the paternal line, he counted on his privileged connection and went to call on Cheng.

sentences.zh: 程方衣鶴氅、華陽巾，憑幾決事，見圜怒詈曰：「是何蟲豸，恃婦力耶！

translations.literal: Cheng was just then wearing a crane-feather cloak and a Huayang cap, leaning on a armrest while deciding affairs; seeing Yuan he cursed in anger, saying: "What kind of vile creature is this, relying on a woman's power!
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was dressed in a crane-feather cloak and Huayang cap, lounging at his writing table while conducting business. At the sight of Ren Huan he burst out in fury: "What vermin is this, trading on his wife's influence!

sentences.zh: 宰相取給於府縣，得不識舊體！」

translations.literal: A chief minister demanding supplies from prefecture and county offices — can he fail to know the old norms!"
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister requisitioning goods from prefectural and county offices — does he not even know the old proprieties!"

sentences.zh: 圜不言而退，是夜，馳至博平，麵訴於莊宗。

translations.literal: Yuan said nothing and withdrew. That night he galloped to Boping and, prostrating himself, pleaded his case before Emperor Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan said nothing and withdrew. That same night he rode hard to Boping, where he kowtowed and laid his grievance before Emperor Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒，謂郭崇韜曰：「朕誤相此癡物，敢辱予九卿。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was angry and said to Guo Chongtao: "I wrongly made this fool chief minister — he dares insult one of my Nine Ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was furious. He said to Guo Chongtao, "I was wrong to make this idiot my chief minister. How dare he humiliate one of my Nine Ministers!"

sentences.zh: 促令自盡。

translations.literal: He urgently ordered Cheng to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Cheng to take his own life at once.

sentences.zh: 崇韜亦怒，事幾不測，賴盧質橫身解之，遂降為右庶子。

translations.literal: Chongtao too was angry; the affair nearly turned unforeseeable, but thanks to Lu Zhi throwing himself between them to resolve it, Cheng was thereupon demoted to Right Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao was angry as well, and the affair nearly spun out of control. Only Lu Zhi's intervention — he literally stepped between them — settled matters. Cheng was demoted to Right Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既定河南，程隨百官從幸洛陽，沿路墜馬，因病風而卒。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhuangzong had settled Henan, Cheng followed the hundred officials in the imperial progress to Luoyang; along the road he fell from his horse and died of a paralytic stroke.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong secured Henan, Cheng accompanied the court on the journey to Luoyang. He fell from his horse along the way and died of a stroke.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng was a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng was a native of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為儒。

translations.literal: In youth he became a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he trained as a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，燕帥劉守光盡率部內丁夫為軍伍，而黥其面，為儒者患之。

translations.literal: In the Tianyou era of Tang, the Yan commander Liu Shouguang conscripted all laborers within his territory into military ranks and tattooed their faces; scholars were distressed by this.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang Tianyou reign, the Yan commander Liu Shouguang drafted every able-bodied man in his domain into the army and branded their faces. Confucian scholars were appalled.

sentences.zh: 多為僧以避之，鳳亦落發至太原。

translations.literal: Many became monks to avoid it; Feng too tonsured his head and went to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Many took tonsure to escape conscription; Feng shaved his head and fled to Taiyuan as well.

sentences.zh: 頃之，從劉守奇奔梁，梁用守奇為博州刺史，表鳳為判官。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Liu Shouqi in flight to Liang; Liang employed Shouqi as prefect of Bozhou and recommended Feng as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he followed Liu Shouqi in defecting to Liang. The Liang court appointed Shouqi prefect of Bozhou and recommended Feng as his adjutant.

sentences.zh: 〈（案：下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: text is missing below.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Editor's note: text is missing below.)〉

sentences.zh: 為鄆州節度判官。

translations.literal: He served as adjutant of the Yanzhou military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as adjutant to the military commissioner of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗聞鳳名，得之甚喜，以為護鑾學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang heard Feng's reputation; obtaining him, he was greatly pleased and appointed him Guardian of the Imperial Procession Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang heard of Feng's reputation and secured his services, he was delighted and made him Guardian of the Imperial Procession Academician.

sentences.zh: 後莊宗即位，拜鳳中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhuangzong acceded, Feng was appointed Palace Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong took the throne, Feng was appointed Palace Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 及入汴，改授禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When they entered Bian, he was reassigned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the court entered Bian, he was reassigned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 莊宗及劉皇后幸張全義第，後奏曰：「妾五六歲失父母，每見老者，思念尊親泣下，以全義年德，妾欲父事之，以慰孤女之心。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited the residence of Zhang Quanyi; the empress submitted: "Your handmaiden lost her parents at five or six; whenever I see an elderly person, I think of my honored parents and weep. Given Quanyi's age and virtue, your handmaiden wishes to treat him as a father, to comfort the heart of a lonely girl."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited Zhang Quanyi's home. The empress said, "I lost my parents when I was five or six. Whenever I see an elderly person, I think of them and weep. Given Zhang Quanyi's age and standing, I wish to honor him as a father — to ease the loneliness of a girl without kin."

sentences.zh: 莊宗許之，命鳳作箋上全義，定往來儀注。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong assented and ordered Feng to compose a formal letter to Quanyi and fix the protocol for their exchanges.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong agreed and ordered Feng to draft the formal letter to Zhang Quanyi and set the ceremonial protocol for their relationship.

sentences.zh: 鳳上書極諫，不納。

translations.literal: Feng submitted a memorial strongly remonstrating; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Feng submitted a forceful memorial of protest. The emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 天成初，置端明殿學士，鳳與馮道俱任其職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, the Hall of Radiant Clarity Academicianship was established; Feng and Feng Dao both held the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng reign the post of Hall of Radiant Clarity Academician was created; Zhao Feng and Feng Dao both held it.

sentences.zh: 時任圜為宰相，為安重誨所傾，以至罷相歸磁州。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Huan was chief minister; he was undermined by An Chonghui, until he was dismissed from the chancellorship and returned to Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ren Huan served as chief minister, but An Chonghui undermined him until he was removed from office and sent back to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 及朱守殷以汴州叛，馳驛賜圜自盡。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou, an express order was sent granting Yuan permission to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bianzhou, an urgent courier was dispatched ordering Ren Huan to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 既而鳳哭謂安重誨曰：「任圜，義士也，肯造逆謀以讎君父乎？

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng wept and said to An Chonghui: "Ren Huan is a man of righteousness — would he contrive rebellion to avenge himself on his lord and father?
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Feng wept and said to An Chonghui, "Ren Huan is a man of honor. Would he truly plot rebellion against his sovereign and father-figure?

sentences.zh: 如此濫刑，何以安國！」

translations.literal: With such indiscriminate punishment, how can the state be settled!"
translations.idiomatic: With punishments this reckless, how can the realm be kept at peace!"

sentences.zh: 重誨笑而不責。

translations.literal: Chonghui smiled and did not rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui only smiled and did not reprove him.

sentences.zh: 是冬，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: That winter he served as acting director of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he served as acting chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 明年春，有僧自西國取經回，得佛牙大如拳，褐漬皴裂，進於明宗。

translations.literal: The next spring a monk returning from the Western Regions with scriptures obtained a Buddha's tooth as large as a fist, brown-stained and cracked, and presented it to Emperor Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring a monk returning from the Western Regions with scriptures brought back a Buddha's tooth the size of a fist — brown, stained, and fissured — and presented it to Emperor Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 鳳揚言曰：「 曾聞佛牙錘鍛不壞，請試之。」

translations.literal: Feng declared publicly: "I have heard that a Buddha's tooth withstands hammering and forging without breaking — please let us test it."
translations.idiomatic: Feng said openly, "I have heard that a Buddha's tooth cannot be broken by hammer or forge. Let us put it to the test."

sentences.zh: 隨斧而碎。

translations.literal: It shattered at once under the axe.
translations.idiomatic: It splintered the moment the axe fell.

sentences.zh: 時宮中所施已逾數千緡，聞毀乃止。

translations.literal: At the time the palace's offerings had already exceeded several thousand strings of cash; on hearing of its destruction they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: By then the palace had already spent several thousand strings of cash on offerings for the relic. When they learned it had been destroyed, the expenditures ceased.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還洛，留知汴州事，尋授中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luoyang, he was left in charge of Bianzhou affairs; soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, Feng was left to administer Bianzhou. Soon afterward he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 〈（李之儀《姑溪居士集》：鳳為《莊宗實錄》，將何挺論劉煦疏不載，句既相，遂引鳳共政事。）〉

translations.literal: (Li Zhi's Collected Works of Master Guniangxi: when Feng was compiling the Veritable Records of Zhuangzong, He Ting's memorial discussing Liu Xu was not included; once both had become chief ministers, Feng was brought in to share in governance.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (According to Li Zhi's Collected Works of Master Guniangxi: while Feng was compiling the Veritable Records of Zhuangzong, He Ting's memorial on Liu Xu was omitted; once both men had become chief ministers, Feng was brought in to share in governance.)〉

sentences.zh: 長興中，安重誨出鎮河中，人無敢言者，惟鳳極言於上前曰：「重誨是陛下家臣，其心終不背主，五年秉權，賢豪俯伏，但不周防，自貽浸潤。」

translations.literal: In the Changxing era, when An Chonghui went out to command Hezhong, no one dared speak; only Feng spoke forcefully before the throne, saying: "Chonghui is Your Majesty's household minister — in his heart he would never turn against his lord. For five years he held power and the worthy bowed before him, but through insufficient caution he brought slander upon himself."
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing reign An Chonghui was sent out to command Hezhong, and no one dared speak for him — except Feng, who argued forcefully before the throne: "Chonghui is Your Majesty's own household servant. At heart he would never betray you. For five years he wielded power and even the great submitted to him, but because he failed to guard against slander, he brought ruin on himself."

sentences.zh: 明宗以為朋黨，不悅其奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong regarded it as factional pleading and was displeased with the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong took this for factional advocacy and was displeased with the memorial.

sentences.zh: 重誨獲罪，乃出邢州節度使。

translations.literal: Chonghui was found guilty and was sent out as military commissioner of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When An Chonghui was condemned, he was sent out as military commissioner of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及閔帝蒙塵於衛州，鳳集賓佐軍校，垂涕曰：「主上播遷，渡河而北，吾輩安坐不赴奔問，於禮可乎？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Min suffered exile at Weizhou, Feng gathered his guests, staff, and military officers and, weeping, said: "Our lord has been driven into exile, crossing the river northward — can we sit at ease and not rush to inquire after him; is that proper in ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min fell into exile at Weizhou, Feng gathered his staff and officers and said through tears, "Our sovereign has been driven from the capital and fled north across the river. Can we sit here in comfort and fail to go to him? Where is the propriety in that?"

sentences.zh: 軍校曰：「唯公所使。」

translations.literal: A military officer said: "We await only your command."
translations.idiomatic: The officers replied, "We are yours to command."

sentences.zh: 將行，聞閔帝遇弑而止。

translations.literal: Just as they were about to set out, they heard that Emperor Min had been murdered and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They were about to depart when word came that Emperor Min had been assassinated, and they abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，召還，授太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was summoned back and granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingtai reign he was recalled to court and appointed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 既而病足，不能朝謁。

translations.literal: Before long his feet were afflicted and he could not attend court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his feet failed him and he could no longer attend court.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，自為蓍筮，卦成，投蓍而歎曰：「吾家世無五十者，而復窮賤；

translations.literal: When his illness was grave he performed divination with yarrow stalks himself; when the hexagram was complete he cast down the stalks and sighed, saying: "In my family no one has ever reached fifty, yet lived in poverty and low station;
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned grave he divined for himself with yarrow stalks. When the hexagram was cast he threw down the stalks and sighed, "No one in my family has ever lived past fifty, and all have died poor and obscure;

sentences.zh: 吾年已五十，又為將相，豈有遐壽哉！」

translations.literal: I am already fifty and have moreover become general and minister — how can there be long life!"
translations.idiomatic: I am already fifty, and I have risen to general and minister — how can I expect a long life!"

sentences.zh: 清泰二年三月卒。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Qingtai he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the second year of Qingtai.

sentences.zh: 鳳性豁達，輕財重義，凡士友以窮厄告者，必傾其資而餉之，人士以此多之也。

translations.literal: Feng's nature was open and generous; he prized righteousness over wealth. Whenever a scholar-friend came to him in distress, he would exhaust his resources to provide for him — for this men greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was open-handed by nature and valued honor over money. Whenever a scholar friend came to him in hardship, he gave freely of whatever he had. Men admired him greatly for it.

sentences.zh: 李愚，字子晦。

translations.literal: Li Yu, courtesy name Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, courtesy name Zihui.

sentences.zh: 自稱趙郡平棘西祖之後，家世為儒。

translations.literal: He claimed descent from the western branch of Pingji in Zhao commandery; his family for generations were scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from the western branch of the Pingji line in Zhao commandery. His family had been Confucian scholars for generations.

sentences.zh: 父瞻業，應進士不第，遇亂，徙家渤海之無棣，以詩書訓子孫。

translations.literal: His father Zhan Ye failed the Presented Scholar examination; encountering turmoil, he moved the family to Wudi in Bohai and instructed his descendants in poetry and the classics.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhan Ye failed the Presented Scholar examination. When turmoil came he moved the family to Wudi in Bohai and raised his descendants on poetry and the classics.

sentences.zh: 愚童齔時，謹重有異常兒，年長方誌學，遍閱經史。

translations.literal: When Yu was in infancy he was grave and careful beyond ordinary children; when he grew older and reached the age of study, he read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child Yu was unusually solemn and self-possessed. When he reached the age of serious study he read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 慕晏嬰之為人，初名晏平。

translations.literal: He admired the character of Yan Ying and at first was named Yan Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Yan Ying and originally bore the name Yan Ping.

sentences.zh: 為文尚氣格，有韓、柳體。

translations.literal: In writing he prized force and structure, with the style of Han and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: His prose prized vigor and structure and showed the influence of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 厲誌端莊，風神峻整，非禮不言，行不苟且。

translations.literal: He hardened his resolve and was dignified; his bearing was stern and composed; he spoke nothing contrary to ritual and acted without laxity.
translations.idiomatic: He disciplined his will and carried himself with dignity. His bearing was austere and composed. He would not speak outside propriety, nor act with casual indifference.

sentences.zh: 愚初以艱貧，求為假官，滄州盧彥威署安陵簿。

translations.literal: Yu at first, because of hardship and poverty, sought a provisional appointment; Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou assigned him secretary of Anling.
translations.idiomatic: At first, pressed by poverty, Yu sought a provisional appointment. Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou made him secretary of Anling.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，服闋，隨計之長安。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed after his father's death, he went with the examination candidates to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his father, he traveled to Chang'an for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 屬關輔亂離，頻年罷舉，客於蒲、華之間。

translations.literal: Just then Guanzhong was in turmoil and dispersal; examinations were suspended year after year, and he sojourned between Pu and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: But Guanzhong was in chaos, and the examinations were suspended year after year. He lived as a guest between Pu and Hua.

sentences.zh: 光化中，軍容劉季述、王奉先廢昭宗，立裕王，五月餘，諸侯無奔問者。

translations.literal: In the Guanghua era, Army Supervisor Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian deposed Emperor Zhaozong and enthroned Prince Yu; for more than five months no feudal lord came to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghua reign, Army Supervisors Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian deposed Emperor Zhaozong and enthroned Prince Yu. For more than five months not a single regional lord came to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 愚時在華陰，致書於華帥韓建，其略曰：「仆關東一布衣耳，幸讀書為文，每見君臣父子之際，有傷教害義之事，常痛心切齒，恨不得抽腸蹀血，肆之市朝。

translations.literal: Yu was then at Huayin and sent a letter to Han Jian, military commissioner of Hua; its gist ran: "Your servant is but a commoner east of the Pass. Fortune has allowed me to read and write; whenever I see affairs between ruler and minister or father and son in which teaching is harmed and righteousness injured, I am constantly pained to the marrow and grind my teeth, wishing I could tear out my entrails and tread blood, and expose it in the marketplace and court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was then at Huayin and wrote to Han Jian, military commissioner of Hua. The letter read in part, "I am only a commoner from east of the Pass, fortunate enough to have learned to read and write. Whenever I see the bonds between ruler and minister, father and son, violated in ways that corrupt teaching and destroy righteousness, I am sick with rage. I would tear out my own entrails and trample them in blood before the court if that could set things right.

sentences.zh: 明公居近關重鎮，君父幽辱月餘，坐視凶逆，而忘勤王之舉，仆所未喻也。

translations.literal: Your Excellency dwells near a vital pass fortress; our lord and father has suffered humiliation in seclusion for more than a month — to sit and watch the wicked rebels and forget the effort to rescue the ruler is what your servant cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a strategic post at the gateway to the capital. Our sovereign has languished in captivity for more than a month, yet you sit by and watch these criminals without raising the banner of loyal rescue. I cannot understand it.

sentences.zh: 仆竊計中朝輔弼，雖有誌而無權；

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that the court ministers, though they have resolve, have no power;
translations.idiomatic: It seems to me that the ministers at court may have the will but not the power;

sentences.zh: 外鎮諸侯，雖有權而無誌。

translations.literal: the regional feudal lords, though they have power, have no resolve.
translations.idiomatic: while the regional lords may have the power but not the will.

sentences.zh: 惟明公忠義，社稷是依。

translations.literal: Only Your Excellency in loyalty and righteousness is one on whom the altars of state may rely.
translations.idiomatic: Only you, my lord, combine loyalty and righteousness — the realm depends on men like you.

sentences.zh: 往年車輅播遷，號泣奉迎，累歲供饋，再復朝廟，義感人心，至今歌詠。

translations.literal: In years past when the imperial carriage was driven into exile, you wept as you welcomed it back, supplied provisions for years, and restored the court and temples — your righteousness moved men's hearts and is sung to this day.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage was driven into exile in years past, you wept as you welcomed it home, supplied the court for years, and restored the ancestral temples. Your loyalty moved the hearts of men and is still praised in song.

sentences.zh: 此時事勢，尤異於前，明公地處要衝，位兼將相，自宮闈變故，已涉旬時，若不號令率先，以圖反正，遲疑未決，一朝山東侯伯唱義連衡，鼓行而西，明公求欲自安，如何決策！

translations.literal: The situation at this time is especially unlike the former; Your Excellency stands at a vital crossroads, your position combining general and minister. Since the upheaval in the palace inner quarters, more than ten days have passed. If you do not take the lead with proclamation and command to plan restoration, hesitating undecided, then one morning the lords east of the mountains may raise righteous banners in alliance, beating drums westward — how will Your Excellency seek your own safety; how will you decide!
translations.idiomatic: The present crisis is graver still. You stand at a strategic crossroads with the rank of both general and minister. More than ten days have passed since the palace coup. If you do not take the lead — issue the call, march first, and restore the rightful order — and if you hesitate, then one day the lords east of the mountains will raise the banner of righteousness in alliance and march west with drums beating. How then will you keep yourself safe? What choice will remain to you?

sentences.zh: 此必然之勢也。

translations.literal: This is the inevitable trend.
translations.idiomatic: That is the inevitable course of events.

sentences.zh: 不如馳檄四方，諭以逆順，軍聲一振，則元凶破膽，浹旬之間，二豎之首傳於天下，計無便於此者。」

translations.literal: Better to dispatch proclamations in all directions, instructing men in rebellion and loyalty; once military prestige is raised, the chief villain will lose heart, and within ten days the heads of the two villains will be transmitted throughout the realm — no plan is more expedient than this."
translations.idiomatic: Better to send proclamations in every direction, teaching men the difference between treason and loyalty. Once your army's name resounds, the chief villain will lose heart. Within ten days the heads of those two usurpers could be displayed throughout the realm. No plan would serve better."

sentences.zh: 建深禮遇之，堅辭還山。

translations.literal: Han Jian treated him with deep courtesy but firmly declined and returned to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian received the letter with great respect, but Yu firmly declined further involvement and returned to his retreat in the hills.

sentences.zh: 天復初，駕在鳳翔，汴軍攻蒲、華，愚避難東歸洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu the imperial carriage was at Fengxiang; the Bian army attacked Pu and Hua, and Yu fled east and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu reign the emperor was at Fengxiang while the Bian army attacked Pu and Hua. Yu fled east to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時衛公李德裕孫延古在平泉舊墅，愚往依焉。

translations.literal: At the time Yangu, grandson of Duke Wei Li Deyu, was at the old villa at Pingquan; Yu went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu's grandson Yangu was living at the old Pingquan estate. Yu went to stay with him.

sentences.zh: 子弟親采梠負薪，以給朝夕，未嘗幹人。

translations.literal: He and the younger men personally gathered acorns and carried firewood to supply daily needs, and never importuned others.
translations.idiomatic: He and the younger members of the household gathered acorns and carried firewood to get by from day to day. He never importuned anyone for help.

sentences.zh: 故少師薛廷珪掌貢籍之歲，登進士第；

translations.literal: In the year when former Junior Mentor Xue Tinggui managed the examination registry, Yu passed the Presented Scholar degree;
translations.idiomatic: In the year when Xue Tinggui, the former Junior Mentor, oversaw the examination registry, Yu passed the Presented Scholar examination;

sentences.zh: 又登宏詞料，授河南府參軍，遂下居洛表白沙之別墅。

translations.literal: he also passed the Hongci examination, was appointed aide of Henan Prefecture, and thereupon settled below Luoyang at a villa at Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: he also passed the Hongci examination, was appointed aide to the Henan prefecture, and settled at a villa in Baisha below Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 梁有禪代之謀，柳璨希旨殺害朝士，愚以衣冠自相殘害，乃避地河朔，與宗人李延光客於山東。

translations.literal: When Liang had a scheme to usurp the throne, Liu Can, seeking to please, killed court gentlemen; Yu, seeing the gentry destroy one another, fled to Hebei and with his clansman Li Yanguang sojourned in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang plotted to seize the throne, Liu Can slaughtered court officials to curry favor. Seeing the scholar-official class turn on itself, Yu fled to Hebei and lived as a guest in Shandong with his clansman Li Yanguang.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝嗣位，雅好儒士，延光素相款奉，得侍講禁中，屢言愚之行高學贍，有史魚、蘧瑗之風。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor of Liang succeeded, he greatly favored Confucian scholars; Yanguang had long been on intimate terms with him and gained appointment to lecture within the palace, repeatedly speaking of Yu's lofty conduct and ample learning, with the air of Shi Yu and Qu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Emperor of Liang succeeded, he greatly favored Confucian scholars. Yanguang, who had long been close to him, gained appointment to lecture within the palace and repeatedly praised Yu's moral stature and erudition, comparing him to Shi Yu and Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 召見，嗟賞久之，擢為左拾遺。

translations.literal: Yu was summoned for audience; the emperor sighed in admiration for a long while and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was summoned to audience. The emperor admired him at length and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 俄充崇政院直學士，或預谘謀，而儼然正色，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Soon he served as Direct Academician of the Chongzheng Hall; though sometimes consulted in planning, he remained stern in countenance and did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Direct Academician of the Chongzheng Hall. Even when consulted on policy he maintained a grave bearing and did not flinch before the powerful.

sentences.zh: 衡王入朝，重臣李振輩皆致拜，惟愚長揖。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Heng entered court, the great ministers Li Zhen and the rest all performed full obeisance; only Yu gave a deep bow with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Heng came to court, senior ministers including Li Zhen all prostrated themselves. Yu alone gave a formal bow with hands folded.

sentences.zh: 末帝讓之曰：「衡王，朕之兄。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor reproved him, saying: "The Prince of Heng is my elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor rebuked him: "The Prince of Heng is my elder brother.

sentences.zh: 朕猶致拜，崇政使李振等皆拜，爾何傲耶！」

translations.literal: Even I perform obeisance; Chongzheng Commissioner Li Zhen and the rest all bow — why are you so arrogant!"
translations.idiomatic: Even I bow to him. Li Zhen and the other commissioners all bow. Why are you so insolent!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下以家人禮兄，振等私臣也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty uses family courtesy toward your brother; Zhen and the rest are private ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "Your Majesty treats your brother with family courtesy. Li Zhen and the others are your personal servants.

sentences.zh: 臣居朝列，與王無素，安敢諂事。」

translations.literal: Your servant stands in the court ranks and has no prior acquaintance with the prince — how dare I fawn in subservience."
translations.idiomatic: I stand in the court ranks and have no prior acquaintance with the prince. How dare I abase myself in flattery?"

sentences.zh: 其剛毅如此。

translations.literal: Such was his firmness.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 晉州節度使華溫琪在任違法，籍民家財，其家訟於朝，製使劾之，伏罪。

translations.literal: Hua Wenqi, military commissioner of Jinzhou, while in office violated the law and confiscated commoners' household property; the family sued at court, an imperial commissioner impeached him, and he confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Wenqi, military commissioner of Jinzhou, broke the law in office by confiscating a commoner's property. The family appealed to court, an imperial commissioner investigated, and Hua confessed his guilt.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝以先朝草昧之臣，不忍加法，愚堅按其罪。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang, because Hua was a minister from the founding days in chaos, was unwilling to apply the law; Yu firmly pressed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor, unwilling to punish a veteran of the founding days, hesitated to apply the law. Yu insisted that the crime be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝詔曰：「朕若不與鞫窮，謂予不念赤子；

translations.literal: The Last Emperor of Liang issued an edict saying: "If We do not investigate thoroughly, men will say We do not care for the common people;
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor issued an edict: "If I do not investigate this thoroughly, men will say I have no care for the common people;

sentences.zh: 若或遂行典憲，謂予不念功臣。

translations.literal: if We then carry out statute and punishment, men will say We do not care for meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: yet if I carry out the full penalty, men will say I have no gratitude for my meritorious servants.

sentences.zh: 為爾君者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: To be your ruler — is it not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: To be your sovereign — is that not a hard thing!

sentences.zh: 其華溫琪所受贓，宜官給代還所訟之家。」

translations.literal: As for the ill-gotten gains received by Hua Wenqi, official funds should be supplied to replace and return them to the suing household."
translations.idiomatic: The property Hua Wenqi seized shall be restored to the aggrieved family from official funds."

sentences.zh: 貞明中，通事舍人李霄傭夫毆僦舍人致死，法司案律，罪在李霄。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era, Palace Herald Li Xiao's hired laborer beat a boarder to death; the legal office applied the statutes and fixed guilt on Li Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming reign, a laborer hired by Palace Herald Li Xiao beat a lodger to death. The legal office applied the statutes and held Li Xiao responsible.

sentences.zh: 愚白：「李霄手不鬥毆。

translations.literal: Yu stated: "Li Xiao's hand did not strike in the brawl.
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued, "Li Xiao did not strike the blow himself.

sentences.zh: 庸夫致死，安得坐其主耶！」

translations.literal: A hired man caused death — how can his master be punished!"
translations.idiomatic: A hired man killed someone — how can his employer be held guilty!"

sentences.zh: 以是忤旨。

translations.literal: For this he offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: For this he offended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 愚自拾遺再遷膳部員外郎，賜緋，改司勳員外郎，賜紫，至是罷職，曆許、鄧觀察判官。

translations.literal: Yu from Remonstrance Censor was promoted again to Vice Director of the Board of Provisioners and granted scarlet robes; he was changed to Vice Director of the Board of Merits and granted purple robes; at this point he was dismissed from office and successively served as observation commissioner adjutant at Xu and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had risen from Remonstrance Censor to Vice Director of the Board of Provisioners with scarlet robes, then to Vice Director of the Board of Merits with purple robes. Now he was removed from office and served successively as adjutant to the observation commissioners of Xu and Deng.

sentences.zh: 初在內職，慈州舉子張礪依焉。

translations.literal: When he was first in an inner court post, the Cizhou examination candidate Zhang Li relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu still held an inner-court post, the Cizhou examination candidate Zhang Li came to study under him.

sentences.zh: 貞明中，礪自河陽北歸莊宗，補授太原府掾，出入崇闥之間，揄揚愚之節概，及言愚之所為文《仲尼遇》、《顏回壽》、《夷齊非餓人》等篇，北人望風稱之。

translations.literal: In the Zhenming era Li returned north from Heyang to Zhuangzong, was appointed a staff officer of Taiyuan Prefecture, and passing in and out among the palace gates praised Yu's integrity and spoke of Yu's essays "Confucius Encounters," "Yan Hui's Longevity," "Boyi and Shuqi Were Not Starving Men," and other pieces; northerners heard the wind and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming reign Zhang Li returned north from Heyang to Zhuangzong's court and was appointed a staff officer in Taiyuan. Moving in court circles, he praised Yu's moral character and spoke of Yu's essays — "Confucius Encounters," "Yan Hui's Longevity," "Boyi and Shuqi Were Not Men Who Starved" — and others. Northerners heard of them and admired Yu from afar.

sentences.zh: 洎莊宗都洛陽，鄧帥俾奏章入朝，諸貴見之，禮接如舊。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong established his capital at Luoyang, the Dengzhou commander had him submit a memorial to court; the great nobles, seeing him, received him with courtesy as of old.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong made Luoyang his capital, the military commissioner of Deng had Yu submit a memorial at court. The great officials received him with the same respect as before.

sentences.zh: 尋為主客郎中，數月，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Director of the Bureau of Receptions; after several months, he was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions. After a few months he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 三年，魏王繼岌征蜀，請為都統判官，仍帶本職從軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Prince of Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu; Yu requested appointment as army superintendent and adjutant, still holding his original post while following the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang, the Prince of Wei, Jiji, marched against Shu. Yu asked to serve as army superintendent and adjutant, retaining his existing post while accompanying the expedition.

sentences.zh: 時物議以蜀險阻，未可長驅，郭崇韜問計於愚，愚曰：「如聞蜀人厭其主荒恣，倉卒必不為用。

translations.literal: At the time public opinion held that Shu was precipitous and dangerous and could not be overrun at full gallop. Guo Chongtao asked Yu for a plan. Yu said: "As I hear, the people of Shu are weary of their lord's dissolute excesses; in haste they surely will not serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Shu was too rugged and perilous for a headlong advance. Guo Chongtao asked Yu's counsel. Yu said, "From what I hear, the people of Shu are sick of their ruler's reckless indulgence. In a crisis they will not stand by him.

sentences.zh: 宜乘其人二三，風馳電擊，彼必破膽，安能守險。」

translations.literal: We should seize upon their disunity, striking like wind and lightning — they will surely lose heart and cannot hold the passes.
translations.idiomatic: We should strike while they are divided, moving like wind and lightning. They will lose heart and cannot hold the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 及前軍至固鎮，收軍食十五萬斛，崇韜喜，謂愚曰：「公能料事，吾軍濟矣！」

translations.literal: When the vanguard reached Guyin and gathered 150,000 hu of army grain, Chongtao rejoiced and said to Yu: "You can forecast events — our army is saved!"
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard reached Guyin and collected 150,000 hu of army grain, Chongtao was delighted. He told Yu, "You read events aright — our army is saved!"

sentences.zh: 招討判官陳乂至寶雞，稱疾乞留在後。

translations.literal: The pacification commissioner and adjutant Chen Yi reached Baoji, claimed illness, and begged to remain in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification adjutant Chen Yi reached Baoji, pleaded illness, and asked to stay behind with the rear guard.

sentences.zh: 愚厲聲曰：「陳乂見利則進，懼難則止。

translations.literal: Yu said in a stern voice: "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he fears hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said sharply, "Chen Yi advances when he sees gain and halts when he fears danger.

sentences.zh: 今大軍涉險，人心易惑，正可斬之以徇。」

translations.literal: Now the great army crosses perilous terrain and morale is easily unsettled — he should be beheaded to warn the troops.
translations.idiomatic: The main army is crossing dangerous ground and morale is easily shaken. He should be executed as an example to the troops.

sentences.zh: 由是軍人無遲留者。

translations.literal: From this no soldier dared linger.
translations.idiomatic: After that no soldier dared hang back.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍書羽檄，皆出其手。

translations.literal: At that time all military dispatches and urgent reports came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time every military dispatch and urgent report came from his hand.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，就拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was appointed on the spot as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, he was immediately appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 師還，明宗即位。

translations.literal: The army returned; Mingzong assumed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned home, and Mingzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 時西征副招討使任圜為宰相，雅相欽重，屢言於安重誨，請引為同列；

translations.literal: At the time the western campaign deputy pacification commissioner Ren Huan served as chief minister; he admired Yu and repeatedly spoke to An Chonghui, requesting that Yu be brought into the same rank;
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan, deputy pacification commissioner of the western campaign and now chief minister, admired Yu and repeatedly urged An Chonghui to bring him into the council of chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 屬孔循用事，援引崔協以塞其請。

translations.literal: but Kong Xun was then in power and brought in Cui Xie to block the request.
translations.idiomatic: but Kong Xun was then in power and brought in Cui Xie to shut the door on the request.

sentences.zh: 俄以本職權知貢舉，改兵部侍郎，充翰林承旨。

translations.literal: Soon, in his existing post he was given provisional charge of the examinations, promoted to Vice Minister of War, and made Hanlin Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was given provisional charge of the civil examinations in his existing post, promoted to Vice Minister of War, and made Hanlin Academician Expositor.

sentences.zh: 長興初，除太常卿，屬趙鳳出鎮邢台，乃拜中書侍郎、平章事，轉集賢殿大學士。
