translations.literal: In the early Changxing era he was appointed Minister of Rituals; as Zhao Feng went out to command Xingtai, Yu was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-administrator of Affairs, then transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall for Collecting Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changxing reign he was made Minister of Rituals. When Zhao Feng departed to command Xingtai, Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-administrator of Affairs, then transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall for Collecting Worthies.

sentences.zh: 長興季年，秦王恣橫，權要之臣，避禍不暇，邦之存亡，無敢言者。

translations.literal: In the final years of Changxing, the Prince of Qin ran rampant; men of power and influence had no leisure to escape disaster, and none dared speak of the realm's survival or ruin.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Changxing the Prince of Qin ran wild. Powerful ministers were too busy saving themselves to speak of the state's survival or ruin.

sentences.zh: 愚性剛介，往往形言，然人無唱和者。

translations.literal: Yu's nature was stern and upright; he often spoke out plainly, yet no one echoed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was stern and uncompromising by nature and often spoke out plainly, yet no one took up his cause.

sentences.zh: 後轉門下侍郎，監修國史，兼吏部尚書，與諸儒修成《創業功臣傳》三十卷。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery, supervised compilation of the national history, and concurrently served as Minister of Personnel; with various scholars he completed the Record of Founding Meritorious Servants in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Vice Director of the Chancellery, put in charge of compiling the national history, and concurrently served as Minister of Personnel. With other scholars he completed the Record of Founding Meritorious Servants in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 愚初不治第，既命為相，官借延賓館居之。

translations.literal: Yu at first had no private residence; once appointed chief minister, the government lent him the Yansin Guesthouse to live in.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had never built a private mansion. Once he was made chief minister, the government lent him the Yansin Guesthouse as his residence.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，詔近臣宣諭，延之中堂，設席惟筦秸，使人言之，明宗特賜帷帳茵褥。

translations.literal: Once when ill, the emperor ordered a nearby minister to convey his sympathy; Yu was received in the central hall, and only matting of coarse straw was laid for seating. When the messenger reported this, Mingzong specially bestowed curtains, bedding, and cushions.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he fell ill, the emperor sent a nearby minister to convey his sympathy. Yu received him in the central hall with only coarse straw matting for a seat. When the messenger reported this, Mingzong specially sent curtains, bedding, and cushions.

sentences.zh: 〈（《職官分紀》云：長興四年，愚病，明宗遣中使宣問。

translations.literal: (Records of Offices and Functions states: In the fourth year of Changxing, Yu fell ill; Mingzong sent a palace envoy to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: (Records of Offices and Functions states: In the fourth year of Changxing Yu fell ill, and Mingzong sent a palace envoy to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 愚所居寢室，蕭然四壁，病榻弊氈而已。

translations.literal: Yu's sleeping chamber was bare on all four walls — only a sickbed with a worn rug.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's bedchamber was bare on all four walls — nothing but a sickbed with a threadbare rug.

sentences.zh: 中使具言其事，帝曰：「宰相月俸幾何？

translations.literal: The envoy fully reported the matter. The emperor said: "How much is a chief minister's monthly salary?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported the whole affair. The emperor said, "How much is a chief minister's monthly salary?

sentences.zh: 而委頓如此。」

translations.literal: Yet he is so exhausted and depleted like this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he is worn down to this state.

sentences.zh: 詔賜絹百匹、錢百千、帷帳什物一十三事。）〉

translations.literal: An edict bestowed one hundred bolts of silk, one hundred thousand cash, curtains, bedding, and thirteen sets of household goods.)〉
translations.idiomatic: An edict bestowed one hundred bolts of silk, one hundred thousand cash, curtains, bedding, and thirteen sets of household goods.)〉

sentences.zh: 閔帝嗣位，誌修德政，易月之制才除，便延訪學士讀《貞觀政要》、《太宗實錄》，有意於致理。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, he sought to cultivate virtuous government; the mourning period had barely ended when he summoned academicians to read the Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Era and the Veritable Record of Emperor Taizong — he had a mind toward bringing order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min succeeded to the throne, he set his heart on virtuous government. Hardly had the mourning period ended when he summoned academicians to read the Essentials of Governance from the Zhenguan Era and the Veritable Record of Emperor Taizong — he meant to bring the realm to good order.

sentences.zh: 愚私謂同列曰：「吾君延訪，少及吾輩，位高責重，事亦堪憂，奈宗社何！」

translations.literal: Yu privately said to his colleagues: "Our lord summons us for counsel yet seldom reaches us ministers of rank; our position is high and responsibility heavy — the matter is worrisome. What will become of the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Yu privately told his colleagues, "Our lord seeks counsel yet seldom reaches us. Our rank is high and our burden heavy — the situation is troubling. What will become of the altars of state!

sentences.zh: 皆惕息而不敢言。

translations.literal: All held their breath and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: All held their breath and dared not answer.

sentences.zh: 以恩例進位左僕射。

translations.literal: By imperial grace he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial grace he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，徽陵禮畢，馮道出鎮同州，愚加特進、太微宮使、宏文館大學士。

translations.literal: In early Qingtai, when rites at Huai Mausoleum were complete, Feng Dao went out to command Tongzhou; Yu was given the special advancement title, made commissioner of the Taibei Palace, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingtai reign, when rites at Huai Mausoleum were complete, Feng Dao departed to command Tongzhou. Yu was granted the special advancement title, made commissioner of the Taibei Palace, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 宰相劉句與馮道為婚家，道既出鎮，兩人在中書，或舊事不便要厘革者，對論不定。

translations.literal: Chief minister Liu Xu was connected by marriage with Feng Dao. After Dao departed to his command, the two men remained in the Secretariat; on certain old matters inconvenient to revise thoroughly, they debated without reaching agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Liu Xu was connected by marriage with Feng Dao. After Dao left for his command, the two men remained in the Secretariat. On certain old arrangements that were awkward to overhaul, they debated back and forth without reaching agreement.

sentences.zh: 愚性太峻，因曰：「此事賢家翁所為，更之不亦便乎！」

translations.literal: Yu's nature was overly severe; he therefore said: "This affair was done by your worthy father-in-law — would it not be more convenient to change it!
translations.idiomatic: Yu was blunt by nature and said, "Your worthy father-in-law set this up — would it not be simpler to change it!

sentences.zh: 句憾其言切，於是每言必相折難，或至喧呼。

translations.literal: Xu resented his pointed words; from then on every remark met with mutual refutation, sometimes rising to shouting.
translations.idiomatic: Xu resented the sharpness of his words. From then on every exchange ended in mutual refutation, sometimes rising to shouting.

sentences.zh: 無幾，兩人俱罷相守本官。

translations.literal: Before long both were dismissed as chief ministers and kept their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both were removed as chief ministers and retained only their original posts.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年秋，愚已嬰疾，率多請告，累表乞骸，不允，卒於位。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Qingtai, Yu was already gravely ill, mostly asking leave on pretext of illness, and repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire — not granted — and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Qingtai Yu was already gravely ill. He mostly stayed away on sick leave and repeatedly memorialized begging to retire, but was not permitted. He died in office.

sentences.zh: 任圜，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Ren Huan, a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖清，成都少尹。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qing was vice governor of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qing served as vice governor of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 父茂宏，避地太原，奏授西河令；

translations.literal: His father Maohong, fleeing disorder, reached Taiyuan and was appointed by memorial as magistrate of Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: His father Maohong fled the turmoil to Taiyuan, where he was appointed by memorial as magistrate of Xihe.

sentences.zh: 有子五人，曰圖、回、圜、團、冏，風彩俱異。

translations.literal: He had five sons, named Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong — each with striking presence.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons — Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong — each with a striking bearing.

sentences.zh: 武皇愛之，以宗女妻團，歷代、憲二郡刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu favored them; he married an imperial clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu favored the family and married an imperial clanswoman to Tuan, who served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭典兵於晉陽，與圜遊處甚洽，及鎮澤潞，請為觀察支使，解褐，賜朱紱。

translations.literal: Li Siyao commanded troops at Jinyang and was on very friendly terms with Huan; when he commanded Ze and Lu, he requested Huan as observation staff officer. Huan entered service and was granted vermilion insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyao commanded troops at Jinyang and was on very close terms with Huan. When Siyao took command of Ze and Lu, he requested Huan as observation staff officer. Huan entered official service and was granted vermilion insignia.

sentences.zh: 圜美姿容，有口辯。

translations.literal: Huan had fine looks and was skilled in eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was handsome and skilled in debate.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭為人間諜於莊宗，方有微隙，圜奉使往來，常申理之，克成友於之道，圜之力也。

translations.literal: Siyao sent agents between Zhuangzong and himself; when there was a slight rift, Huan as envoy passed back and forth and constantly argued on behalf of reconciliation, completing the path of fraternal friendship — this was Huan's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Siyao sent intermediaries between himself and Zhuangzong. When a slight rift opened between them, Huan shuttled back and forth as envoy and constantly argued for reconciliation, restoring their bond of friendship — this was Huan's achievement.

sentences.zh: 及丁母憂，莊宗承製起復潞州觀察判官，賜紫。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother, Zhuangzong, by imperial rescript, recalled him to service as adjutant to the Lu observation commissioner and granted purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his mother, Zhuangzong recalled him to service by imperial rescript as adjutant to the Lu observation commissioner and granted him purple robes.

sentences.zh: 常山之役，嗣昭為帥，卒於軍，圜代總其事，號令如一，敵人不知。

translations.literal: In the Changshan campaign, Siyao served as commander and died in the army; Huan took over command of all affairs — orders went forth as one, and the enemy did not know.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changshan campaign Siyao served as commander and died in the field. Huan took over command of all affairs. Orders continued as before, and the enemy never knew.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞之，倍加獎賞。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard of it and added rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong heard of it, he doubled his rewards.

sentences.zh: 是秋，復以上黨之師攻常山，城中萬人突出，大將孫文進死之，賊逼我軍，圜麾騎士擊之，頗有殺獲。

translations.literal: That autumn, again with the Shangdang army he attacked Changshan; ten thousand men burst out of the city; the great general Sun Wenjin died in the action; the rebels pressed our army; Huan directed cavalry to strike them and killed or captured quite a number.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he again led the Shangdang army against Changshan. Ten thousand men burst from the city; the great general Sun Wenjin fell in the fighting. As the rebels pressed our army, Huan directed cavalry against them and killed or captured a good number.

sentences.zh: 嘗以禍福諭其城中，鎮人信之，使乞降。

translations.literal: He once used fortune and calamity to instruct those in the city; the garrison men believed him and sent envoys to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He once preached fortune and calamity to those in the city. The garrison believed him and sent envoys to sue for surrender.

sentences.zh: 及城潰，誅元惡之外，官吏鹹保其家屬，亦圜所庇護焉。

translations.literal: When the city fell, aside from executing the chief culprits, officials were all preserved along with their families — also under Huan's protection.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, apart from executing the ringleaders, all officials and their families were spared — also through Huan's protection.

sentences.zh: 莊宗改鎮州為北京，以圜為工部尚書兼真定尹、北京副留守，行留守事。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong changed Zhenzhou to the Northern Capital; he made Huan Minister of Works, concurrently true prefect of Zhending and deputy northern regent, administering regent affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong redesignated Zhenzhou as the Northern Capital and made Huan Minister of Works, concurrently true prefect of Zhending and deputy northern regent, administering regent affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，郭崇韜兼鎮，改行軍司馬，充北面水陸轉運使，仍知府事。

translations.literal: The next year Guo Chongtao concurrently commanded the region; Huan was changed to army superintendent, made northern water-and-land transport commissioner, and still governed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Guo Chongtao took concurrent command of the region, Huan was made army superintendent and northern water-and-land transport commissioner, while still governing prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，歸朝，守工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he returned to court and remained Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tongguang he returned to court and retained the post of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 崇韜伐蜀，奏令從征，西蜀平，署圜黔南節度使，懇辭遂止。

translations.literal: When Chongtao campaigned against Shu he memorialized that Huan should follow the expedition; when western Shu was pacified he appointed Huan military commissioner of Qiannan — Huan earnestly declined and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao campaigned against Shu he memorialized that Huan should accompany the expedition. After western Shu was pacified he appointed Huan military commissioner of Qiannan, but Huan earnestly declined and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 魏王班師，行及利州，康延孝叛，以勁兵八千回劫西川。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Wei's army withdrew, having reached Lizhou, Kang Yanxiao rebelled, turning back with eight thousand crack troops to raid western Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince of Wei's army withdrew, having reached Lizhou, Kang Yanxiao rebelled and turned back with eight thousand crack troops to raid western Chuan.

sentences.zh: 繼岌聞之，夜半命中使李廷安召圜，圜方寢，廷安登其床以告之，圜衣不及帶，遽見繼岌。

translations.literal: Jiji heard of it; at midnight he ordered the palace envoy Li Ting'an to summon Huan. Huan was asleep; Ting'an climbed onto his bed to tell him; Huan dressed without waiting for his belt and hastened to see Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiji heard of it, he sent the palace envoy Li Ting'an to summon Huan at midnight. Huan was asleep; Ting'an climbed onto his bed to tell him. Huan dressed without waiting for his belt and rushed to see Jiji.

sentences.zh: 繼岌泣而言曰：「紹琛負恩，非尚書不能制。」

translations.literal: Jiji wept and said: "Shaochen has betrayed his grace — only you, Vice Director, can restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji wept and said, "Shaochen has betrayed us. Only you, Vice Director, can bring him to heel.

sentences.zh: 即署圜為招討副使，與都指揮使梁漢顒等率兵攻延孝於漢州，擒之。

translations.literal: He immediately appointed Huan deputy pacification commissioner; with commander-in-chief Liang Hanyong and others he led troops to attack Yanxiao at Hanzhou and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed Huan deputy pacification commissioner. With commander-in-chief Liang Hanyong and others he led troops against Yanxiao at Hanzhou and captured him.

sentences.zh: 旋至渭南，繼岌遇害。

translations.literal: Soon they reached Weinan; Jiji was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they reached Weinan, where Jiji was murdered.

sentences.zh: 圜代總全師，朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: Huan took over the entire army and presented himself at court in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan took command of the entire army and presented himself at court in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘉其功，拜平章事，判三司。

translations.literal: Mingzong commended his merit and appointed him Co-administrator of Affairs, with charge of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong commended his achievement and appointed him Co-administrator of Affairs with charge of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 圜揀拔賢俊，杜絕幸門，百官俸入為孔謙減折。

translations.literal: Huan selected the worthy and talented and shut the door on favor-seekers; officials' salaries had been reduced and discounted by Kong Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Huan selected the worthy and talented and shut the door on favor-seekers. Officials' salaries had been cut and discounted under Kong Qian.

sentences.zh: 圜以廷臣為國家羽儀，故優假班行，禁其虛估，期月之內，府庫充贍，朝廷修葺，軍民鹹足。

translations.literal: Huan held that court ministers were the state's ceremonial standard, so he treated the official ranks generously and forbade inflated valuation; within one month the treasury was full, the court was refurbished, and army and people were all provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Huan held that court ministers were the ceremonial face of the state, so he treated the official ranks generously and forbade inflated valuation. Within a month the treasury was full, the court was refurbished, and both army and people were provided for.

sentences.zh: 雖憂國如家，而切於功名，故為安重誨所忌。

translations.literal: Though he loved the state as his own home, he was keen on fame and achievement, and therefore was resented by An Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Though he cared for the state as for his own household, he was eager for fame and achievement, and therefore earned An Chonghui's resentment.

sentences.zh: 嘗與重誨會於私第，有妓善歌，重誨求之不得，嫌隙自茲而深矣。

translations.literal: Once he met Chonghui at a private residence; there was a courtesan skilled in song; Chonghui requested her but could not obtain her — from this their rift grew deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met Chonghui at a private residence where a courtesan skilled in song was present. Chonghui asked for her but could not have her. From that their rift grew deep.

sentences.zh: 先是，使人食券，皆出於戶部，重誨止之，俾須內出，爭於御前，往復數四，竟為所沮，

translations.literal: Previously, envoy ration certificates all issued from the Ministry of Revenue; Chonghui stopped this and required them to come from the inner palace; they disputed before the emperor, back and forth several times, and in the end Huan was blocked,
translations.idiomatic: Previously envoy ration certificates had all issued from the Ministry of Revenue. Chonghui stopped this and required them to come from the inner palace instead. They disputed before the emperor back and forth several times, and in the end Huan was thwarted,

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：安重誨與圜爭於上前，往復數四，聲色俱厲。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: An Chonghui and Huan disputed before the emperor, back and forth several times, both voice and expression fiercely stern.
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: An Chonghui and Huan disputed before the emperor back and forth several times, both voice and expression fiercely stern.

sentences.zh: 上退朝，宮人問上：「適與重誨論事為誰？」

translations.literal: After the emperor left court, a palace woman asked: "With whom were you just now debating with Chonghui?
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor left court, a palace woman asked him, "With whom were you just now arguing with Chonghui?

sentences.zh: 上曰：「宰相。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The chief minister."

sentences.zh: 宮人曰：「妾在長安宮中，未嘗見宰相、樞密奏事敢如是者，蓋輕大家耳！」

translations.literal: The palace woman said: "When I was in the Chang'an palace, I never saw a chief minister or privy council commissioner dare to present business in such a manner — they must look down on Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: The palace woman said, "When I was in the Chang'an palace, I never saw a chief minister or privy council commissioner dare to present business like that. They must look down on Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 上愈不悅。）〉

translations.literal: The emperor grew even more displeased.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew even more displeased.)〉

sentences.zh: 因求罷三司。

translations.literal: Huan thereupon requested dismissal from the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Huan thereupon asked to be relieved of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，除太子少保致仕，出居磁州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired, living at Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and retired to live at Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 及朱守殷叛，重誨乘間誣其結構，立遣人稱製就害之，乃下詔曰：「太子少保致仕任圜，早推勳舊，曾委重難，既退免於劇權，俾優閑於外地，而乃不遵禮分，潛附守殷，緘題罔避於嫌疑，情旨頗彰於怨望。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled, Chonghui seized the opportunity to falsely accuse him of collusion; he immediately sent a man bearing an imperial rescript to put him to death, and issued an edict saying: "Retired Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Ren Huan, long commended as an old meritorious servant, once entrusted with grave duties — having retired from pressing power he was granted ease in a distant post; yet he did not observe ritual propriety and secretly joined Zhu Shouyin; sealed letters without avoiding suspicion — his intent and language quite plainly showed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled, Chonghui seized the chance to falsely accuse Huan of collusion. He immediately sent a man bearing an imperial rescript to put him to death and issued an edict: "Retired Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent Ren Huan, long honored as an old meritorious servant and once entrusted with grave duties, was granted ease in a distant post after retiring from pressing power. Yet he failed to observe ritual propriety and secretly joined Zhu Shouyin. His sealed letters did not avoid suspicion, and their tone plainly showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 自收汴壘，備見蹤由，若務含宏，是孤典憲，尚全大體，止罪一身。

translations.literal: Since the capture of the Bian ramparts, his tracks have been fully seen; if We sought magnanimous tolerance, We would fail the canonical law; yet wishing to preserve the larger principle, We punish only his person.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capture of the Bian ramparts his movements have been fully traced. To show magnanimous tolerance would betray the canonical law. Yet wishing to preserve the larger principle, We punish only his person.

sentences.zh: 宜令本州於私第賜自盡。」

translations.literal: He should be ordered at his private residence in his prefecture to be granted death by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted death by his own hand at his private residence in his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 圜受命之日，聚族酣飲，神情不撓。

translations.literal: On the day Huan received the order, he gathered his clan for a hearty drink; his spirit did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Huan received the order, he gathered his clan for a hearty drink. His composure did not falter.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，製贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the Qingtai era an imperial rescript posthumously made him Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qingtai era an imperial rescript posthumously made him Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 子徹，仕皇朝，位至度支郎中，卒。

translations.literal: His son Che served the imperial court, rising to Director of the Bureau of Revenue, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che served the imperial court, rising to Director of the Bureau of Revenue, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：革、說承舊族之胄，佐新造之邦，業雖謝於財成，罪未聞於昭著，而乃為權臣之所忌，顧後命以無逃，靜而言之，亦可憫也。

translations.literal: The court historian says: Ge and Shuo inherited the credentials of old clans and assisted a newly founded state; their achievement fell short of completion and their guilt was not conspicuously known — yet they were resented by powerful ministers and perished by later command with no escape. Spoken quietly, one may pity them.
translations.idiomatic: The court historian writes: Dou Luge and Wei Shuo inherited the standing of old clans and served a newly founded state. Their work fell short of completion and no conspicuous guilt was laid against them, yet powerful ministers resented them and they perished by later command with no escape. Considered quietly, their fate is pitiable.

sentences.zh: 盧程器狹如是，形渥攸宜。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng's capacity was so narrow — his station and emolument were quite fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng's talents were so narrow — his rank and salary suited him well enough.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳、李愚，咸以文學之名，俱踐岩廊之位，校其貞節，愚復優焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng and Li Yu both rode the name of literary learning to tread the hall of cliff — comparing their integrity, Yu again had the advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng and Li Yu both rose on the reputation of literary learning to seats in the highest council. Comparing their integrity, Yu again had the advantage.

sentences.zh: 任圜有縱橫濟物之才，無明哲保身之道，退猶不免，籲可悲哉！

translations.literal: Ren Huan had talent to traverse and aid the world, yet lacked the way of the wise who preserve themselves; even in retirement he could not escape — ah, how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan had the talent to move across the realm and aid the world, yet lacked the wisdom to preserve himself. Even in retirement he could not escape — ah, how lamentable!
